audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Numbers / Bemidbar camp purity, restitution, and suspected-adultery ordeal text tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for camp removal, restitution plus fifth, priestly portions, jealousy/suspected-adultery ordeal, written curse, bitter water, and outcome language. Strong anti-misogyny, anti-coercion, and anti-reenactment safeguards required.

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,

verses.restored: Command children of Israel that they send from camp everyone afflicted with scale-disease, everyone with discharge, and everyone unclean by dead soul/life.

familiar.text: Command the children of Israel, that they put out of the camp every leper, and every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead:

verses.restored: Male and female you shall send; outside camp you shall send them, so they do not make their camps unclean, in whose midst I dwell.

familiar.text: Both male and female shall ye put out, without the camp shall ye put them; that they defile not their camps, in the midst whereof I dwell.

verses.restored: Children of Israel did so and sent them outside camp; as YHWH spoke to Moses, so children of Israel did.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel did so, and put them out without the camp: as the LORD spake unto Moses, so did the children of Israel.

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,

familiar.text: Then they shall confess their sin which they have done: and he shall recompense his trespass with the principal thereof, and add unto it the fifth part thereof, and give it unto him against whom he hath trespassed.

familiar.text: And every man’s hallowed things shall be his: whatsoever any man giveth the priest, it shall be his.

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,

familiar.text: And the priest shall charge her by an oath, and say unto the woman, If no man have lain with thee, and if thou hast not gone aside to uncleanness with another instead of thy husband, be thou free from this bitter water that causeth the curse:

verses.restored: But if you have turned aside under your husband and become unclean, and a man besides your husband has given his emission in you—

familiar.text: But if thou hast gone aside to another instead of thy husband, and if thou be defiled, and some man have lain with thee beside thine husband:

familiar.text: And this water that causeth the curse shall go into thy bowels, to make thy belly to swell, and thy thigh to rot: And the woman shall say, Amen, amen.

verses.restored: Priest shall write these curses in scroll and wipe them into bitter water.

familiar.text: And the priest shall write these curses in a book, and he shall blot them out with the bitter water:

verses.restored: He shall make woman drink bitter water bringing curse, and water bringing curse shall enter her for bitterness.

familiar.text: And he shall cause the woman to drink the bitter water that causeth the curse: and the water that causeth the curse shall enter into her, and become bitter.

familiar.text: Then the priest shall take the jealousy offering out of the woman’s hand, and shall wave the offering before the LORD, and offer it upon the altar:

familiar.text: And the priest shall take an handful of the offering, even the memorial thereof, and burn it upon the altar, and afterward shall cause the woman to drink the water.

verses.restored: But if woman has not become unclean and is clean, then she shall be free and shall conceive seed.

familiar.text: And if the woman be not defiled, but be clean; then she shall be free, and shall conceive seed.

familiar.text: This is the law of jealousies, when a wife goeth aside to another instead of her husband, and is defiled;

translation_notes: Verses 2-4 are camp-boundary instructions in a sanctuary-centered wilderness setting; they must not justify abandoning sick or disabled people.
Restitution in verses 5-10 applies to man or woman and requires confession, principal return, and added fifth.

The suspected-adultery ordeal is an ancient patriarchal jealousy procedure centered on the wife, with no parallel ordeal for a husband. Preserve this asymmetry for critique rather than smoothing it away.
The ritual may function as a controlled priestly procedure that prevents immediate private retaliation, but it remains coercive and must never be reenacted.
Outcome language involving belly/thigh is textually and medically uncertain and requires deep lexical audit.
Verse 31's asymmetry must not be used to excuse controlling, jealous, or abusive husbands.
safety_note: Do not reenact, imitate, prescribe, or spiritually replicate the Numbers 5 ordeal. Do not use it to coerce women, accuse partners without evidence, excuse jealousy, shame infertility, blame survivors, or authorize abuse. Preserve it as a difficult ancient patriarchal legal-ritual text under explicit ethical critique.
